title: Vegetation, nests and biological hazards
audience: Trainees and workers on the solar panel cleaning track, working under supervision, who clean arrays that have vegetation, birds, insects or droppings around them.
learningOutcomes: Identify biological hazards around a PV array, including nests, droppings and vegetation.
Separate routine cleaning of droppings from the removal of nests and the trimming of vegetation, which are outside the cleaning scope.
Apply a check, stop and refer decision to an active nest or a vegetation problem that affects access.

instruction.heading: Biological hazards around arrays
instruction.body: Arrays are often mounted where birds, bats, wasps, spiders and other animals shelter or nest. Vegetation can grow over the array and shade it, and leaves or debris collect at the edges and in gutters. These biological hazards can cause stings, bites, slips and contamination. Before access, look at the array and its surroundings for nests, droppings, hives and vegetation that could reach the work area, and record what you see.

instruction.heading: Nests and wildlife
instruction.body: Do not disturb an active nest. NSW's biodiversity law (the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016) covers native birds, with listed exceptions. Check the rule for the state before any removal. Where a nest is active or its status is unknown, keep the work away from it, record its position, and refer the removal to the owner or the appropriate authority. A cleaning worker does not remove nests under this course.

instruction.heading: Droppings and routine hygiene
instruction.body: Bird droppings on panels are a routine part of the cleaning job when the method and the PPE allow it. Wear the PPE the job pack names, avoid breathing dust or spray, wash hands after the job, and keep the work area clean. Droppings that are dried and dusty need care, because the dust can carry organisms. Where the droppings are heavy or the area is enclosed, stop and check the job plan before continuing.

instruction.heading: Vegetation that affects access or shading
instruction.body: Vegetation that shades the array, or grows over the array edge, is not part of the cleaning scope unless the owner separately authorises trimming. Trimming vegetation near an electrical installation can bring electrical and fall risks. Record the vegetation and its effect, and refer the trimming to the owner and to a qualified person. Do not cut vegetation with a tool from the roof or the array edge. The NSW code of practice on work near overhead and underground electric lines (in force from 22 May 2026) says a worker should assume an overhead line is live unless the supply authority has confirmed otherwise in writing. Refer any branch that touches a line to the network operator, and keep people out of the area.

instruction.heading: Stop and refer
instruction.body: Stop and refer when an active nest is within the work area, when a hive or swarm is present, when a wasp or spider presence causes a risk, when vegetation blocks a safe access route, or when a worker has an allergic reaction. Keep people clear, record the location, and refer to the owner and to the appropriate person. Seek urgent medical care for any sting or bite that causes a reaction.

instruction.heading: Licence and authority boundary
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant an electrical licence, pest control licence, tree-trimming authority or any wildlife permit. Vegetation work and nest removal are outside the cleaning course.

procedure: Look at the array and its surroundings for nests, droppings, hives and vegetation before access.
Record any active or unknown nest, its position and its risk to the work area.
Check the state or territory wildlife rule before any nest is disturbed, and refer nest removal to the owner.
Wear the PPE that the job pack names for droppings, and avoid breathing dust or spray.
Record vegetation that affects access or shading, and refer any trimming to the owner and a qualified person.
Stop and refer if an active nest, hive or swarm is in the work area, or if a worker reacts to a sting or bite.
Record the observations, the decision and the people told.

workedExamples.situation: A worker finds an active bird nest under the lower row of panels. The cleaning would need the worker to reach under the array.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not disturb the nest or reach under the array. Record the nest's position, keep the work away from it, and check the state wildlife rule. Refer the removal to the owner, and let the owner decide on the proper removal route. Clean the rows that can be reached safely if the owner agrees.

workedExamples.situation: A tree branch has grown over the top edge of the array and is touching the mounting frame, and the owner asks the cleaner to trim it while cleaning.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Trimming is not part of the cleaning scope, and trimming near an electrical installation brings electrical and fall risks. Record the branch and its contact with the frame, and refer the trimming to the owner and a qualified person. The cleaner may clean the array only as the scope allows.

equipmentAndPpe: Biological hazard checklist for the array and its surroundings
PPE for droppings as specified in the job pack, including eye and respiratory protection where the job calls for it
Barrier or marker for an active nest or hive
Referral template for nest removal and vegetation trimming

commonErrors.error: Disturbing a nest to get access to the array.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep away from the nest, record it, and refer the removal.

commonErrors.error: Trimming a branch from the array edge.
commonErrors.prevention: Vegetation trimming is outside the scope unless separately authorised.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning dry droppings without any PPE.
commonErrors.prevention: Wear the PPE the job pack names and avoid breathing the dust.

commonErrors.error: Ignoring a sting or allergic reaction.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, seek urgent medical care, and record the incident.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: In New South Wales, the biodiversity law covers native birds, with listed exceptions (NSW environment page updated 7 September 2026).
Licence notice: This lesson does not grant an electrical licence, pest control licence, tree-trimming authority or wildlife permit. Nest removal and vegetation trimming are outside this course.

qualityStandard: The array and its surroundings are checked for nests, droppings, hives and vegetation before access.
No active nest is disturbed, and the removal is referred.
PPE for droppings is worn as the job pack names.
Vegetation that affects access or shading is recorded and referred.
documentationEvidence: Biological hazard observation record with positions and photographs
Nest or hive record with the referral and the state rule checked
PPE record for the droppings task
Vegetation record and referral for any trimming
summary: Check the array and its surroundings for biological hazards before access.
Do not disturb an active nest, and check the state wildlife rule before any removal.
Vegetation trimming is outside the cleaning scope unless separately authorised.
This lesson grants no pest control, tree-trimming or wildlife authority.

knowledgeChecks.question: A bird nest is found under the array. What should the worker do?
options: Remove it quickly with a stick or hose before the job starts today on site
Check the state wildlife rules, avoid disturbing an active nest, and refer
Disturb it to clear the space for the ladder and the crew to pass today
Spray it with a chemical to clear the nest and the area below it today

knowledgeChecks.question: Trimming vegetation that shades the array is:
options: Part of the cleaning price for every job at the site and the roof
Always included in the cleaning job and the price quoted here
Not part of the cleaning scope unless separately authorised
A solar service that the worker performs on the roof each time

knowledgeChecks.question: Bird droppings on a panel are a:
options: Warranty claim against the manufacturer of the panel itself
Signal to use high pressure on the panel and the frame today
Reason to skip the panel and move on to the next row today
Routine hygiene matter, handled as the job plan directs

knowledgeChecks.question: An active nest blocks a safe access route to the array. What should the worker do?
options: Move the nest with a stick to clear the route for the crew and the ladder today
Stop, record the position, and refer to the owner and the appropriate authority
Continue around it and keep working on the route to the array on the day of the job
Spray the area with the cleaning product on the route and the ladder today
